lines.cap: He kept going, for twenty nine years, after it was over.
lines.say: He kept going, for twenty nine years, after it was over.

lines.cap: Hiroo Onoda. A Japanese officer, sent to a jungle island in the Philippines in 1944.
lines.say: Hiroo Onoda. A Japanese officer, sent to a jungle island in the Philippines in 1944.

lines.cap: His orders: never surrender. Keep fighting, whatever happens.
lines.say: His orders: never surrender. Keep fighting, whatever happens.

lines.cap: The war ended in 1945. Leaflets fell from the sky. Family letters. Newspapers. He thought they were all tricks.
lines.say: The war ended in 1945. Leaflets fell from the sky. Family letters. Newspapers. He thought they were all tricks.

lines.cap: So he stayed. Rain, heat and hiding, year after year. His men died or gave up, one by one. His group killed about thirty islanders.
lines.say: So he stayed. Rain, heat and hiding, year after year. His men died or gave up, one by one. His group killed about thirty islanders.

lines.cap: In 1974, a young Japanese traveller found him, and asked him to come home.
lines.say: In 1974, a young Japanese traveller found him, and asked him to come home.

lines.cap: He only came out when his old commander flew in, and told him in person. The war is over.
lines.say: He only came out when his old commander flew in, and told him in person. The war is over.

lines.cap: Twenty nine years, for an order nobody remembered giving.
lines.say: Twenty nine years, for an order nobody remembered giving.
